Saturday — seal the largest drafts first:
1. Gather medium-density adhesive foam weatherstripping, paintable exterior-grade silicone or latex-silicone caulk, a caulk gun, scraper or putty knife, mild cleaner, rags, and—if needed—a small dehumidifier or moisture absorber.
2. With the window closed, use your hand or a strip of tissue to locate drafts. Air at the moving sash, meeting rail, or side channels indicates a sash leak; air where the frame meets the wall or trim indicates a trim/frame leak.
3. Scrape away loose exterior caulk, clean and dry the seams, and apply a fresh bead to trim-to-wall or frame gaps. Smooth it with a damp finger.
4. Let the caulk cure for the time stated on the tube—typically a few hours to overnight. Avoid disturbing it while it sets.

Sunday — tighten the sash:
1. If the draft is at the sash, apply adhesive foam weatherstripping along the vertical sides where the sash meets the tracks and along the horizontal meeting rail where the upper and lower sashes meet when closed. If the upper sash is loose, seal its top edge as well.
2. Keep the bottom edge clear so drainage is not blocked, and place the strips only where the sash presses when locked.
3. Open and close the window once to confirm it still operates smoothly.
4. If the draft is actually at the trim, touch up only the missed or poorly bonded spot with a little more caulk and let it dry.

After sealing — prevent moisture buildup:
• Pull curtains back slightly so air can circulate around the glass.
• Air out the room briefly if condensation appears, and avoid blocking airflow at the window.
• Run a small dehumidifier or use a moisture absorber if needed, especially overnight.
• Wipe condensation from the window area regularly so mold does not get a foothold.
